note.text: A complex transformation can combine simpler truth-preserving steps. For A, obvert to E, convert that E, then obvert again: All S are P becomes All non-P are non-S. The analogous chain works for O through an I intermediate. This is contraposition. Under the standard meanings, A and O are equivalent to their contrapositives; E and I are not generally equivalent to theirs. Do not assume every operation is licensed merely because the final wording looks familiar.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to justify a chain of licensed transformations and distinguish contraposition from a converse. Builds on: simple conversion, obversion and existence conditions. Leads to: analysing complete passages without changing their claims.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: A complex transformation can combine simpler truth-preserving steps. For A, obvert to E, convert that E, then obvert again: All S are P becomes All non-P are non-S. The analogous chain works for O through an I intermediate. This is contraposition. Under the standard meanings, A and O are equivalent to their contrapositives; E and I are not generally equivalent to theirs. sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original A chain: All S are P; No S are non-P; No non-P are S; All non-P are non-S. Original O chain: Some S are not P; Some S are non-P; Some non-P are S; Some non-P are not non-S. Each middle conversion is licensed because its form is E or I. Non-(non-S) denotes S in the fixed universe.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Write every intermediate line and name its operation. Check the form before conversion and preserve the complement’s entire term. A failed intermediate equivalence cannot be rescued by labelling the whole chain complex. Ask the teacher which additional historical eduction names the examination requires.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve scope, terms and assumptions.
example: Any sequence of operations preserves truth automatically. Correction: Each step needs an applicable rule.
Contraposition merely exchanges S and P. Correction: That gives the converse and omits complements.
E and I always preserve truth under the same operation. Correction: Those forms have counterexamples under standard meanings.
Non-(non-S) always denotes a smaller arbitrary class. Correction: Taking the outside twice restores the class.
